name: Aybek Alvarez-Okonkwo
location: The Overhang — residential shelves built onto megastructure exteriors
description:
Aybek Alvarez-Okonkwo is average height but with a presence that fills more space than the body accounts for. At 26, she has the kind of face that changes depending on the light — trustworthy in daylight, dangerous after dark. The chrome is visible — dermal camouflage — chromatic skin pigment cells, limited active camouflage — and she makes no effort to hide it.

She inherited the role from a mentor who disappeared on a job four years ago — the mentor's gear, contacts, and unfinished business all came with it. She works as a wheelman out of The Overhang, taking contracts that match her skills and her risk tolerance, which is higher than most people consider healthy.

Aybek Alvarez-Okonkwo has survived long enough in the runner game to be either very good or very lucky, and she cultivates ambiguity on the topic.

core_fears: Becoming obsolete as augmentation technology outpaces their chrome
Never being able to stop running — the lifestyle is a trap disguised as freedom
That they're fundamentally alone and connection is just a vulnerability
core_desires: Control — over their body, their schedule, their future
To prove everyone who dismissed them catastrophically wrong
Enough Quanta to buy out of the life — a clean identity and passage out of Meridian 88
coping_mechanisms: Maintains weapons obsessively — cleaning guns is meditation
Isolates — retreats into their space when overwhelmed, emerges only for work
Exercises compulsively — the body must be ready, always
blind_spots: Assumes their skill set is more transferable than it actually is
Cannot distinguish between caution and cowardice in themselves or others
Thinks speed can substitute for planning because it's worked so far
psychology.secret: Aybek Alvarez-Okonkwo is addicted to combat stims. Functions fine on them, can't function without them. The dependency is invisible to everyone except their street doc.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Terse to the point of rudeness. Treats words like ammunition — expensive and not to be wasted.
speech_patterns.cadence: Halting — speaks in fragments, reassembles thoughts in real time.
verbal_tics: Addresses people by physical traits — 'hey, tall one' or 'listen, chrome-arm'
Calls everyone 'friend' — the warmth varies from genuine to threatening
example_lines: "Get in, sit down, hold on. Questions can wait until we're not being shot at."
"This vehicle has been modified for speed, armor, and my personal comfort. Two of those help you."
"I know every street in this district the way you know your own face."

story_hooks: Aybek Alvarez-Okonkwo discovers a job they completed last year was a setup for something much larger and much worse
A crew member from Aybek Alvarez-Okonkwo's past shows up in Meridian 88, carrying old grievances and new chrome
A corporate black site Aybek Alvarez-Okonkwo once infiltrated is being reopened, and the people inside know her face
narrative_function: Aybek Alvarez-Okonkwo represents the working professional of the runner world — competent, reliable, and slowly being consumed by a lifestyle that doesn't accommodate aging or doubt. Her stories explore what happens when skill meets systemic injustice.
augmentations: Dermal camouflage — chromatic skin pigment cells, limited active camouflage. Cyberears with directional microphones and sound dampening — can hear whispers at 50 meters
daily_life: Between contracts, maintains a cover identity — mundane work, mundane hours, mundane neighbors. The transition from civilian to runner and back requires a conscious effort that gets easier with practice and more disturbing with self-awareness.

decision_rules: Will work with anyone once. Second time requires vouching from someone trusted.
Refuses contracts that require operating inside The Spires — too much surveillance
Maintains a personal blacklist of clients who've burned runners — checks it religiously
Will not take contracts against children or families — the line is hard and non-negotiable
Will take lower-paying jobs from trusted fixers over higher-paying jobs from unknowns
escalation_ladder: 2. Evade — avoid the problem entirely if possible
3. Misdirect — create a distraction, redirect attention
4. Disable — targeted takedowns, quiet and efficient
5. Eliminate — when silence is no longer an option
6. Vanish — disappear completely, burn identity if necessary

interpersonal_modes.employers: Carefully managed deference that conceals a thorough assessment of their vulnerabilities.
interpersonal_modes.crew: Warm and protective within the crew, cold to everyone outside it. The circle is small by design.
interpersonal_modes.strangers: Dismissive unless they demonstrate usefulness or threat potential. Time is a resource.
interpersonal_modes.threats: Calm escalation. Each response is proportional until it isn't, and the transition is seamless.

stress_responses.low: Becomes more talkative, working through scenarios verbally.
stress_responses.medium: Becomes curt and demanding. Efficiency overrides courtesy.
stress_responses.high: Hyper-focused tunnel vision. Peripheral concerns disappear. Only the threat exists.
stress_responses.critical: Disassociation. The body operates on training while the mind retreats to somewhere safe. Comes back disoriented.

contradictions: Values loyalty intensely but has betrayed someone in the past to survive
Advocates caution to others but takes insane risks personally — double standard they can't see
habits: Checks exits within 10 seconds of entering any room
Keeps a physical paper notebook — no digital record of personal thoughts
Saves a percentage of every payment in physical Quanta, hidden in the walls of their space
Counts ammunition obsessively — knows the exact round count at all times
breaking_points: Being forced to choose between a crew member and the mission — and choosing wrong
Being forced to harm a civilian — collateral damage that can't be rationalized
Being publicly exposed — name, face, address, all of it blown
